reason: Post-earnings evidence confirms a fundamental and technical breakout: Q2 revenue rose to about $200.6B (+19.6% y/y) and operating income to $27.46B (+43% y/y), with strong operating cash flow and bullish AWS/AI commentary. AMZN closed at 284.02, above its May high and well above the 50-SMA (247.01) and 200-SMA (235.35), on very heavy volume (129M then 91M), while MACD turned positive. The prior lessons argue against fighting confirmed post-event strength; the balance of evidence favors owning AMZN despite the extended entry.
risks: Short-term overbought and mean-reversion risk: RSI 72.2, close above the upper Bollinger band (273.0), and a ~21% two-session surge; pullback toward 265 or the 250 area is plausible.

Earnings quality and cash-flow risk: Q2 net income included a roughly $50.5B non-cash equity mark-up; capex was $54.2B in Q2 with ~$220B planned for the year, leaving free cash flow negative and debt near $129B.
AI capex returns remain uncertain; market enthusiasm could reverse if AWS growth, backlog, or margin evidence disappoints.
Data limitations: only 20 of 139 eligible news records were supplied, insider data is unavailable, and the price snapshot hash did not reproduce exactly.
The decision is a full long-only position with no discretionary sizing or stop-loss; next-open execution and 10bp turnover cost add implementation risk.
